root.name: Pterodactyl Defense: Queen Pterodactyl, Quiet Line

overview: Black has fianchettoed and hit d4 with ...c5. After the quiet 4.e3 Black usually plays ...Qa5 (the Queen Pterodactyl), pinning the knight on c3 and eyeing the c3 and d2 squares, then ...Nc6 and ...Nf6. White develops with Nge2, Bd2 and Qb3 or a3, aiming to keep a space edge. The game is a manoeuvring fight with a hypermodern flavour.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quietly with Nge2, Bd2, d5 or dxc5 to keep a small space edge.
Break the pin with Bd2 or Qb3 and use the c4 pawn and the extra centre space.

black_ideas.idea: Pin the c3 knight with ...Qa5, develop with ...Nc6 and ...Nf6, and hit d4 with ...cxd4.
Exchange pawns and use the Bg7 on the long diagonal and the half-open c-file.

typical_structures.structure: White d4/c4/e3 pawns against Black c5 and g6 fianchetto, often with an exchange on d4 and a half-open c-file.

character.notes: Hypermodern manoeuvring; queen on a5 invites tactics but the quiet line avoids the forcing ones.

gambit.notes: No material is offered in the main line.

soundness.notes: Playable for Black; no clear refutation.

structure.notes: Centre in tension at c5 and d4; may become Benoni- or Maróczy-like, so undecided.

approach.notes: Played by some strong players in the Modern complex but rarely; treated as a respectable sideline.

level.notes: The queen sortie and tension need careful timing, but not much memory.

character.reason: Quiet hypermodern play, not known for forcing sequences or for being hard to attack.

soundness.reason: A rare but playable Black set-up.

structure.reason: The centre tension at c5 and d4 can resolve several ways.

approach.reason: A rare sideline in the Modern family, still respectable.

level.reason: Needs judgement on the queen's placement rather than memory.

plans.reason: Black fianchettoes and attacks White's centre with ...c5.
